title: shell_run leaves stdin an open pipe: pathless rg/grep-style commands block forever
wanted_capability: shell_run should spawn commands with stdin connected to /dev/null (or an immediately closed pipe) unless a caller explicitly supplies stdin, so tools that read stdin when it is not a tty (ripgrep with no path argument, grep, cat, jq without files, and the rtk rewrites of them) fail fast or search the cwd instead of blocking indefinitely; and supervision should surface a long-running tool as a hang candidate to the orchestrator (idle_seconds already exists, a threshold nudge or auto-timeout on the shell tool would close the loop). Observed 2026-08-16: a glm-5.3 bro dispatched with a lane cwd ran `rtk rg -n --no-heading '<pat>' --type rust | head -80` (no path); the host-side rg process sat asleep at 0 CPU on fd 0 for 15 minutes until the orchestrator killed it by hand.
missing_primitive: stdin=/dev/null default (or explicit stdin control) on shell_run; hang detection/timeout on shell tools
fallback_used: Orchestrator killed the rg process on the host, then bro_steer'd the worker to always pass an explicit path or `< /dev/null` and prefer code.* / file tools for repo search.
notes: Recurrence tally 2026-08-16: four hangs across two glm-5.3 workers in one afternoon (three on the docs worker, one on the M9a worker), each 7-15 minutes of dead time until the orchestrator killed the host-side rg by hand. Steering the worker to always pass a path helped but did not fully generalize (one worker read `-g '*.md'` as a path). The fix belongs in shell_run, not in prompts.
